Container.Name: bfbackup-peer
Container.Overview: BFBackup peer: receives backups from (or sends files to) a BFBackup controller (install bfbackup-controller on one server first). Needs only the controller address and the token from the controller's web UI (Peers, Add peer). No ports to open on this server; the peer connects out to the controller. Backups land as plain files and folders: no repository, no archive format. Made for Unraid, works on any Linux Docker host.
Container.Changes: See https://github.com/delsol-ger/bfbackup/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md. Each release says whether the peers need the update too.
Container.Requires: A BFBackup controller (bfbackup-controller) on another server.

Config.Name: Controller address
Config.Description: IP or host name of the controller, optionally with :port (default 7701). Example: 192.168.1.10

Config.Name: Token
Config.Description: Token from the controller web UI (Peers, Add peer). Starts with bfb1.

Config.Name: Appdata
Config.Description: Hook scripts (hooks/) and connection.log, which shows every connection attempt to the controller.

Config.Name: Storage
Config.Description: Where backups are stored (or files are read from): user shares (/mnt/user) and unassigned disks (/mnt/disks), same paths as on the host. The single array disks and pools are only used to move deleted files into the trash without copying; they are never shown. Use 'Allowed roots' to narrow what the controller may touch.

Config.Name: Allowed roots
Config.Description: Comma-separated folders inside the container the controller may access. Narrow this (e.g. /mnt/user/Backups) to limit what the controller can see.

Config.Name: Owner UID for written files
Config.Description: 99 = nobody on Unraid. Empty: leave as root.

Config.Name: Transport
Config.Description: tls: encrypted (default). plain: unencrypted, only for weak CPUs on fast links; the controller must allow it.
